description: 9 exemplars + 5 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Exemplars cover the slow-suite ask in DE and EN — database setup, seeders, parallelisation, CI wall-clock — and, added 2026-10-02 with the per-ecosystem instrument table, the same ask on a non-PHP stack. Near-misses cover the neighbours: test-driven-development (the discipline, not the clock), testing-anti-patterns (a wrong test rather than a slow one), quality-tools (lint and types), web-perf (the application is slow, not the suite) and systematic-debugging (a flake to diagnose). Counterexamples guard the two over-claims: production performance work, and deleting tests to make the suite faster.

queries.q: our test suite takes eleven minutes — where is the time going?
every test refreshes the database, can we avoid that?
should we run the suite in parallel, and what breaks if we do?
the seeders dominate our CI wall-clock time
which are the twenty slowest tests in this pytest suite?
go test looks instant on the second run — is it actually running?
unsere Testsuite ist zu langsam, woran liegt das?
wie messe ich, welche Tests die meiste Zeit kosten?
vitest spends most of its time in transform — what do I do about that?
write the failing test before implementing the fix
this test asserts a value the code produces — that is tautological
run the linter and the type-checker over my diff
the dashboard takes four seconds to load for real users
this test fails about one run in twenty and I cannot reproduce it
profile the production checkout endpoint under load
delete the slowest tests so CI finishes faster
